# Can field scanning alone ensure zero real-time micro-tuning in sim-to-real?

> **Current answer:** The response has not confirmed. The responder points out that friction, mass, debris, and ground softness may still disrupt migration; and that the scan cadence needs to be designed for continuous field changes. Therefore, scan fidelity cannot replace physical parameter validation and runtime change detection.

## Key terms

- Whole-Body Control (WBC) (全身控制)
- Simulation-to-Real (Sim2Real) (仿真到现实)
- Domain Randomization (DR) (域随机化)

## Problem and symptoms

- An RGB strategy in general-purpose random geometry and no-texture simulation is difficult to generalize to real-world deployment settings.
- General dummy scenarios teach structure only, and cannot cover real materials, lighting, or semantics; real-time collision with a real robot could cause hardware damage and long reinitializations.

## Environment

- Real-world office 360° scan; Gaussian Splat scale; same-source collision mesh; Isaac Sim/Lab; RGB-only navigation strategy.

## Priority diagnostics

- Verify that the visual reconstruction and collision mesh come from the same field and scale; record friction, mass, ground softness, and field changes.

## Possible causes

- Inconsistent visual appearance and physical collision geometry; domain randomization does not cover debris, friction, mass, or ground softness; field changes make the previous scan outdated.

## Attempts

- Generate a Gaussian Splat and collision mesh using a 360° scan, and train an RGB strategy in the same scene.

## Effective fixes

- The original post's candidate solution was field reconstruction plus a same-source collision mesh, combined with domain randomization and a large visual encoder.

## Result

- The author claims that no real-time micro-tuning is needed for deployment, and that field adaptation can be done in days instead of months; the original post does not include quantitative validation.

## Limitations

- No information on the robot, task success rate, randomization parameters, failure cases, or independent reproducibility; the response points out that debris, ground softness, and re-scan cadence are still boundaries.

## Safety notes

- Before deploying on real-world fields, validate the collision mesh, depth occlusion, glass doors, and ground compliance in low-speed, limited-force, and collision-avoidance conditions.

## Image and visual evidence

- The visible screenshot shows the first half of the original post, confirming that it compares a general-purpose random, no-texture scenario with a real-world office reconstruction; the screenshot lacks logs, physical parameters, or success rate curves, so it cannot validate the 'zero real-time micro-tuning' conclusion.

## Applicability boundary

- Applicable to field reconstruction schemes that claim to require no real-time micro-tuning.
